method: Fresh mpmath(110-digit) model: F_U(t)=prod_i[1-p_i(1-F((t-lam_i)/th_i)^a_i)]. st checked via S_U-S_V, rh via reversed-hazard rtil=f/F difference; all premises (M_n co-monotonicity, T-transform chain, >=^w ascending-sums per Example 5.1, >=^p printed Def 2.2(d) <=-products, baseline C-conditions) re-verified independently.

convention_notes.weak_supermajorization: Paper's Example 5.1 confirms x >=^w y = ascending partial sums of x >= those of y (lambda=(1,2.5,5) >=^w mu=(0.5,2,3)).
convention_notes.p_larger: Def 2.2(d) as printed (verified raw UTF-8 U+2264): x >=^p y iff ascending prefix products of x <= those of y. Theorem 4.3(i) premise '1/theta >=^p 1/delta' then means asc-prod(1/theta) <= asc-prod(1/delta) <=> desc-prod(theta) >= desc-prod(delta). NOTE: the paper's own proof of 4.3(i) requires the opposite direction (needs asc-prod(1/theta) >= asc-prod(1/delta) to drive s=-ln theta weak-supermajorization), so the printed definition conflicts with the printed proof's usage.
convention_notes.MOQL_baseline_defect: The paper's Section 5.2 'Marshall-Olkin extended quasi Lindley' baseline F=(1-q)/(1-(1-a)q), q=((b+1+dx)/(b+1))e^{-dx}, at the printed parameters a=0.1,b=-0.9,d=0.8 is NOT a distribution function: q(x)=(1+8x)e^{-0.8x} exceeds 1 for 0<x<~2.2, giving F(0.25)=1.203, F(1)=1.153, and F^alpha reaching 2.12. The hazard rate is negative on an interval. No premise-fulfilling instance may use this object as 'the baseline distribution function' under (A1).
